title: Reclaim Chat vertical space and surface composer tools more cleanly
description:
Problem: the live `/chat` review showed the header and model controls taking a large amount of vertical room before any conversation content appears. The native attachment input, context status, send-on-enter checkbox, disabled step/stop icons, and full-width send button create a visually heavy composer even when there are no messages.

Desired outcome: Chat prioritizes the message stream and active composer while keeping model, diagram, attachment, trace, and sidebar controls easy to discover.

Scope:
- In scope: compact model/diagram control placement, composer toolbar consolidation, attachment affordance alignment with TSK-0122, disabled control presentation, sidebar toggle discoverability, and empty-state spacing.
- Out of scope: changing chat persistence, model invocation, or agent behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- The message stream gets noticeably more first-viewport space on narrow screens.
- Model/profile/diagram controls remain discoverable but do not dominate the route header.
- Composer actions have a consistent hierarchy and avoid redundant full-width treatment where compact controls would be clearer.
- Empty chat state still communicates readiness without wasting vertical space.

Validation:
- Capture `/chat` screenshots with and without sidebar open at narrow and desktop widths.
- Run focused browser checks for model selection, sidebar toggle, composer focus, attachment affordance, and send-button availability.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 live visual review: `/chat` header/model controls plus composer controls consumed much of the first viewport before useful message content.
